notes: PSA 11 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.35. Prostate volume 32 mL. csPCa 0.66.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for rising PSA and a new PI-RADS 5 lesion on MRI despite prior negative biopsy results.

Long-standing referral for rising PSA levels, now 11.0 ng/mL, with a velocity of 5.55 ng/mL/year. The patient is a retired police officer, married, and lives with his partner. He is a non-smoker, abstains from alcohol, and cycles 20 km twice weekly. His IPSS score is 0, indicating no significant lower urinary tract symptoms. He has a history of chronic shoulder pain managed in the pain clinic and recently had a routine chest X-ray and cataract review. He reports no new neurological or musculoskeletal symptoms. An interpreter for Arabic is requested for the next visit.

On DRE, the prostate is smooth, symmetrical, and non-tender, consistent with a cT1c stage. General examination reveals a well-nourished man with a BMI of 23.6. Vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 121/69 mmHg and heart rate of 85 bpm.
